Nxeon hosting platform, code at /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TS/Prisma/Postgres). I'm planning two things: (a) migrating paid game servers off "dedicated IPv4 per order" toward "shared IP + port remap" by default, and (b) adding a new $2.99/mo "Dedicated IPv4" add-on that a customer can select in the deploy wizard OR purchase later for an already-deployed server. I already know (from a prior investigation) that `server.wantsDedicatedIp` exists on the Server model, `dedicated_ip_default` is a global settings toggle (lib/settings.ts, default true), and `allocateDedicatedIp`/OVH failover-IP integration exists in the provisioning worker (worker/index.ts). I need to understand the FULL existing lifecycle of dedicated IPs and any similar recurring add-on, so I can design the new feature to reuse existing patterns rather than invent new ones.

Please investigate and report on:

1. **VPS deploy wizard's existing "Dedicated IPv4" add-on** — find where `dedicatedIp` (or similar) appears as a customer-selectable option in `components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx` and its pricing. Is it a one-time charge, or a recurring monthly line added to the server's renewal amount? Trace it from the wizard checkbox through `lib/order.ts` (or wherever VPS orders are placed) to see how the add-on's price gets baked into what the customer is billed at renewal. Find the actual dollar price/settings key for this add-on today.

2. **Any existing "add a paid feature to an already-deployed server" flow.** Look at `lib/actions-server.ts` and the customer server-detail dashboard (e.g. `app/dashboard/servers/[id]` or similar) for any action that lets a customer add something (extra disk, backup tier, a dedicated IP, docker, malware scanner) to a server AFTER it's already deployed — not just at order time. I need the exact mechanism: does it charge immediately via Stripe/wallet, does it update `Server` fields, does it enqueue a new worker job (e.g. to actually allocate the IP or trigger `provision`-adjacent network changes on a live VM), and how does it affect the next renewal invoice amount.

3. **`allocateDedicatedIp` and OVH integration cost/limits.** Find `allocateDedicatedIp` in worker code and any related OVH API wrapper (grep for "ovh", "failover", "virtualMac"). Is there a finite pool of dedicated IPs Nxeon has purchased from OVH (i.e., a real per-IP cost to Nxeon), or are they provisioned on-demand from OVH's API with no local pool constraint? This matters for whether "sell an add-on IP" needs an availability/limits check.

4. **Where recurring per-server add-on pricing lives and how renewal billing recalculates it.** Find whatever computes a server's renewal charge (search for "renewalQuote" or similar, mentioned in a prior session as a function name) and confirm whether it's a pure function that reads `Server` fields (backupTier, extraDiskGB, wantsDedicatedIp, etc.) to compute the total — this determines whether adding a new billable boolean/field to `Server` is enough for renewal billing to "just work" or whether extra plumbing is needed.

5. **Existing settings-driven pricing constants** — find how prices like backup-tier cost, extra-disk-per-GB cost are stored (a `lib/settings.ts` key, a hardcoded constant, or a DB-driven pricing table) so a new $2.99/mo dedicated-IP price can follow the same convention (admin-configurable vs hardcoded).

Report file paths with line numbers. This is read-only investigation — do not propose changes, just report what exists.

125	  // falling back to the live setting for legacy/monthly rows. Both halves resolve
126	  // the same number, so an annual sub renews at the sold rate.
127	  const annualPct = server.annualDiscountPct ?? prices.annualDiscountPct;
128	  // Extra root disk is billed EVERY cycle at the current per-GB price. Game plans
129	  // are a flat all-in price and never carry the add-on lines.
130	  const extraDiskMonthlyCents = isGame ? 0 : extraDiskCentsAt(server.extraDiskGB, prices.extraDiskPerGbCents);

132	  // Paid backup retention (Plus) rides alongside extra disk: billed every cycle at
133	  // the current admin price, and — like every add-on line — NOT carried by a game
134	  // plan (renewalCharge's game branch is flat all-in, so game servers are never
135	  // sold a paid backup tier; see lib/backup-upgrade.ts's game guard).
136	  const backupMonthlyCents = isGame ? 0 : backupTierMonthlyCents(server.backupTier, prices.backupPlusCents);
137	  const backupCents = backupMonthlyCents * months;
138	  // A game plan's `priceCents` is its MONTHLY base (every seed is `termMonths: 1`).
139	  // Divide by the plan's own term so an admin plan configured as, say, a 3-month
140	  // bundle still yields a per-month rate; then price the customer's chosen term
141	  // through the SAME formula VPS uses. For a monthly game server this is exactly
142	  // `priceCents`; an ANNUAL game server renews at 12× that, less the annual discount.
143	  const gameMonthlyCents = isGame
144	    ? Math.round(server.gamePlan!.priceCents / Math.max(1, server.gamePlan!.termMonths))

162	      : termPriceCents(gameMonthlyCents, months, annualPct);

174	  const taxRatePercent =

179	    netCents,

## 2. Existing "add a paid feature to an already-deployed server" flows

Two full implementations exist to model the new add-on on. **No such flow exists yet for dedicated IP** (confirmed by exhaustive grep — no `ADD_DEDICATED_IP`/similar job type, no `nxeonDedicatedIp`-style Stripe metadata key, nothing in `lib/actions-server.ts`).

### Pattern A — Extra disk (`DISK_EXPAND`, has a worker job) — closest analog for dedicated IP
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/disk-expand.ts`: `diskExpandQuote()` (pure quote/validation) + `applyDiskExpand()` (atomic: wallet debit + Invoice(PAID) + `Job{type:"DISK_EXPAND"}` create, all in one `$transaction`, lines 150-221). **`Server.extraDiskGB` is deliberately NOT bumped here** — only the worker advances it after the disk really grows (line 27-29, comment), so a failed job doesn't bill for undelivered storage.
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-disk.ts` `expandServerDisk()` (server action, `"use server"`): ownership check, email-verification purchase gate, rate limit (5/10min, line 26-27), `walletSplit()` to decide card-vs-wallet, either `createDiskExpandCheckout()` (Stripe) or `applyDiskExpand()` directly.
- Card path: `/opt/nxeon/lib/stripe.ts` `createDiskExpandCheckout()` (line 358) puts `{serverId, addGB, chargeCents}` in Stripe metadata key `nxeonDiskExpand`; classified in `classifyCheckoutSession` (line 685-700) and dispatched by the confirm route to call `applyDiskExpand` with the exact `chargeCents` collected — this is how "charges immediately via Stripe or wallet" is implemented without double-charging (comment block lines 15-30 explains the invariant).
- Worker side: `worker/index.ts` line 1343 `DISK_EXPAND: diskExpand` handler; line 1361 comment confirms the handler advances `Server.extraDiskGB` only after the disk actually grows; line 1440 `reconcileFailedDiskExpand` refunds on terminal failure.
- **Renewal effect**: none needed beyond `Server.extraDiskGB` — `renewalCharge` reads it directly every cycle (§4).

### Pattern B — Backup tier upgrade (`backupTier`, NO worker job — column flip only)
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/backup-upgrade.ts`: `backupUpgradeQuote()` + `applyBackupUpgrade()` — same shape as disk-expand but **wallet-only in the MVP** (no Stripe checkout function exists for it — comment lines 16-18) and **no Job is created**: it directly `tx.server.update({ backupTier, backupKeep, autoBackup: true, backupIntervalHours })` inline (lines 171-179), because retention is "just a column the next scheduled prune reads" (comment lines 19-21).
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-backup.ts` `upgradeServerBackupTier()`: ownership check, verification gate, quote, wallet-balance pre-check (rejects with a dollar figure if card isn't wired for this path), `applyBackupUpgrade()`.
- **Upgrade-only, no downgrade**, both patterns.

### Which pattern fits dedicated IP
Dedicated IP allocation is **not** a pure DB column — it requires calling OVH (`ovhApi.createVirtualMac`, polling for the vMAC to bind) and then reconfiguring the live Proxmox VM's `net0`/`ipconfig0` (exactly what `worker/index.ts` lines 902-916 do during `unsuspend`). That is real, potentially slow, retriable hypervisor work — **the DISK_EXPAND pattern (worker job) is the right template, not the backup-tier pattern.** A new `JobType` (e.g. `ADD_DEDICATED_IP`) alongside a `lib/dedicated-ip-upgrade.ts` (mirroring `disk-expand.ts`) would fit the codebase's established conventions. The Proxmox reconfigure logic already exists nearly verbatim at `worker/index.ts` lines 902-916 (unsuspend path) and could be reused/extracted.

There is currently **no dashboard UI button** for any of this on the server-detail page beyond what's referenced in `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` for disk/backup (lines ~380-560, `renewalQuote` import at line 30, `renewQuote` computed line 129) — no dedicated-IP upsell card exists there today.

## 3. `allocateDedicatedIp` / OVH integration — pool model and cost

File: `/opt/nxeon/lib/dedicated-ip.ts`

- **There IS a finite local pool with a real per-IP cost to Nxeon** — `DedicatedIp` DB table, statuses `FREE`/`PENDING`/`ASSIGNED`, `purpose` `CUSTOMER`/`INTERNAL`. `OVH_IP_UNIT_COST_CENTS = 239` (line 39) is "what OVH actually bills per additional/failover IPv4" — a real recurring infra cost tracked for the accounting dashboard (`dedicatedIpPoolMonthlyCostCents()`, lines 134-144: `total * OVH_IP_UNIT_COST_CENTS`, counting every pooled IP whether assigned or not).
- **Pool is populated by `syncDedicatedIpPool()`** (lines 83-126), which pulls OVH's already-purchased failover/additional IPv4 blocks (`ovhApi.ips()`), and imports any not already tracked, not already vMAC-bound, and not carrying a live iptables DNAT rule (`hasLiveDnatRule`, lines 20-31 — guards against re-handing out an IP that's secretly serving production traffic, per the incident note in the comment).
- **This is NOT "provision on-demand from OVH with no local constraint."** `allocateDedicatedIp()` (lines 163-215) atomically claims a `FREE`+`CUSTOMER` row from the **existing local pool** inside a `$transaction` (lines 185-193) — if none is `FREE`, it returns `null` (no OVH order is placed on the fly). Ordering *more* IPs from OVH is a **manual admin step** — confirmed by the admin panel: `dedicated_ip_autoreplenish` toggle is labeled "Notify admins... (ordering more IPs stays a manual step)" (`/opt/nxeon/components/admin/settings/DedicatedIpPanel.tsx` line 32).
- **Consequence for the new add-on: yes, an availability/limits check is needed**, and the codebase already has the exact idiom for it — `freeCount()` (lines 130-132) / the inline `db.dedicatedIp.count({status:"FREE", purpose:"CUSTOMER"})` used to gate the wizard checkbox (`app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx` line 60/106). A post-deploy "buy a dedicated IP" action should use the same check before offering/charging, and must handle `allocateDedicatedIp` returning `null` (pool empty) gracefully — same as `worker/index.ts` line 461-468 already does at provision time (falls back to NAT rather than failing the whole provision).
- Idempotency: `allocateDedicatedIp` first checks if the server already holds an `ASSIGNED` IP with a bound vMAC and returns it unchanged (lines 175-178) — safe to call again on retry.
- `releaseDedicatedIp()` (lines 218-235) returns an IP to the pool on suspend/delete, deleting the OVH vMAC.
- Reverse-DNS: `setDedicatedReverse()` (lines 238-242).

Full lifecycle touchpoints in the worker (`/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts`):
- `PROVISION` (lines 455-469): `wantDedicated = server.wantsDedicatedIp || (await _settingBool("dedicated_ip_default", true))` — **note the OR**: the per-server intent flag is ORed with a global default that itself defaults to `true`.
- `unsuspend`/`suspend` (lines 883-960): releases the IP back to the pool on suspend, re-allocates + reconfigures Proxmox `net0`/`ipconfig0` on unsuspend, with a NAT-fallback reconfigure if no IP could be re-acquired (lines 917-933) — this is the template for a live "add IP to a running server" job.

**Relevant to the user's part (a) migration plan**: `/opt/nxeon/lib/game-order.ts` line 277 already hardcodes `wantsDedicatedIp: false` for every game-server order. **However**, because of the OR at `worker/index.ts` line 460/899, a game server *still* gets a dedicated IP by default today, since the global `dedicated_ip_default` fallback is `true` and there is no override anywhere that special-cases `gamePlanId` against that global setting. Also notable: `dedicated_ip_default` has **no entry in `SETTINGS_DEFAULTS`** in `lib/settings.ts` and **no admin UI control** (not present in `DedicatedIpPanel.tsx`) — its only defined value is the inline literal `true` at the two `worker/index.ts` call sites. Migrating games to shared-IP-by-default will need to either flip that global default, or add explicit game-aware logic at those two OR sites (both currently identical one-liners, a good sign they're meant to be edited together).

## 4. `renewalCharge` — the renewal pricing engine

File: `/opt/nxeon/lib/renewal-charge.ts` — **confirmed pure function**, no DB/side effects. Single source of truth used everywhere (`lib/renewal-quote.ts`, `worker/billing.ts`, `app/dashboard/page.tsx`, `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx`, `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx`, `lib/actions.ts`, `lib/actions-payment-method.ts`).

- Signature: `renewalCharge(server: PricedServer, prices: RenewalPrices): RenewalCharge`
- `PricedServer` (lines 51-69) needs: `termMonths, extraDiskGB, plan{name,priceCents}, gamePlan|null, dedicatedIp: unknown|null, backupTier, annualDiscountPct?`
- `RenewalPrices` (lines 77-104) is **all required fields** (`ipMonthlyCents, extraDiskPerGbCents, backupPlusCents, annualDiscountPct, taxRatePercent?`) — deliberately, so no call site can silently omit an admin price and fall back to a stale default (comment lines 71-76).
- The dedicated-IP line specifically (line 166-169): `(server.dedicatedIp ? prices.ipMonthlyCents * months : 0)` — **it bills off whether the server actually HAS a `DedicatedIp` row (`dedicatedIp: unknown | null`, the relation), not off the `wantsDedicatedIp` intent flag** — explicit comment: "a NAT-fallback server must never be charged for an IP it never received."
- Game plans are entirely excluded from every add-on line (`isGame` branch is flat all-in, lines 110, 128-137, 163-171).

**Answer to the "does adding a new billable boolean just work" question**: **Not quite "just add a field and done."** `renewalCharge` is pure and reads whatever shape you pass it (a `Server` row today already supplies `dedicatedIp` via its Prisma relation, e.g. `lib/actions.ts` line 980: `const hasDedicatedIp = !!(await db.dedicatedIp.findFirst({ where: { serverId } }))`, then passed at line 998 as `dedicatedIp: hasDedicatedIp ? {} : null`). Since the dedicated-IP add-on's renewal line **already exists and is wired end-to-end today** (it's just priced at 0 by default), turning on the $2.99/mo charge for the *existing* deploy-time flag needs **zero code changes** to `renewalCharge` — only flipping the `dedicated_ip_price_cents` setting. If the new post-deploy purchase path reuses the same `DedicatedIp` relation as its "is this billable" signal (which it should, to match the "bill off what the server actually has" invariant), **no `renewalCharge`/`RenewalPrices` changes are needed at all** — every call site already threads `dedicatedIp`/`ipMonthlyCents` through. The only new plumbing needed is upstream of `renewalCharge`: the post-deploy purchase action/job itself (§2), not the pricing engine.

## 5. Settings-driven pricing convention

All three recurring add-on prices follow the **same convention**: an admin-configurable DB setting (via `lib/settings.ts` `SETTINGS_DEFAULTS`), read through a small dedicated accessor function that clamps to a non-negative integer, never a hardcoded constant used directly in a money path.

| Add-on | Setting key | Default | Accessor | Admin UI |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Extra disk | `extra_disk_gb_price_cents` (settings.ts:212) | `"10"` ($0.10/GB/mo) | `extraDiskPerGbCents()` (disk-expand.ts:56-59) | `BillingPanel.tsx` line 116-119 |
| Backup Plus tier | `backup_plus_price_cents` (settings.ts:217) | `"299"` ($2.99/mo) | `backupPlusMonthlyCents()` (backup-upgrade.ts:49-52) | **not exposed in any admin panel** (DB-only today) |
| Dedicated IP | `dedicated_ip_price_cents` (settings.ts:238) | `"0"` (included) | `dedicatedIpMonthlyCents()` (dedicated-ip.ts:65-68) | `DedicatedIpPanel.tsx` line 12-19 (already has a "Monthly price (cents)" `TextField`) |

Each accessor is explicitly documented as the "single source of truth for order/expansion(or upgrade)/renewal/display" so all paths agree (see comments at disk-expand.ts:51-59, backup-upgrade.ts:43-48, dedicated-ip.ts:50-68). Each also has an env-var/module-constant fallback for the settings-table default itself (e.g. `DEDICATED_IP_PRICE_CENTS = Number(process.env.DEDICATED_IP_PRICE_CENTS ?? 0)`, dedicated-ip.ts:48), but the *settings row* always wins at runtime via `getSettingInt`.

**Convention for the new $2.99/mo price**: it doesn't need a new setting at all — `dedicated_ip_price_cents` and its admin UI (`DedicatedIpPanel.tsx`) already exist and already read/write exactly this value; setting it to `299` is the whole "pricing" side of the feature. If a *separate* price were wanted for "add-on after deploy" vs "at deploy," that would be a deviation from how disk/backup do it (same price both times) and would need a new key following the identical `getSettingInt(key, default)` + doc-comment pattern.
